rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each listed source carries a freshness STAMP, not just a to-do.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L153: `[checked:2026-07-30 result:OK due:2027-01-30]` on the Willison 'Designing agentic loops' URL. 2026-07-30 + 6 months = 2027-01-30 exactly — this is the literal 'checked+6mo' computation §11a bans by name: 'Never checked+6mo — re-opening a March post in August confirms it still says what it said; it does not make the world it describes younger, and the arithmetic grants a three-weeks-from-stale source a fresh year, most confidently on the sources someone bothered to re-check.' The stamp's own prose disclaims the durable-account carve-out ('Not a §2a durable-account carve-out... this piece describes a general technique'), so DUE was owed as publication+6mo (already passed: 2025-09-30 + 6mo ≈ 2026-03-30) or `cohort`, not a fresh forward date computed off the check date. Harm is real, not just rule-shaped: `source-freshness.sh --target <cohort-date>` audits by comparing `due` against the target date, so this stamp will read as fresh (no WARN/BLOCK) until 2027-01-30 even though the underlying evidence is already outside its own stated window — the exact false-green the rule exists to prevent. Contrast: the OTHER changed stamp in this same diff (L149, claude-code-on-the-web) moved FROM the same checked+6mo pattern (was due:2027-02-15 = 2026-08-15+6mo) TO the compliant `due:cohort` for a capability claim — that one is a genuine fix, evidence the author knows the correct pattern, which makes the Willison line read as an oversight rather than a considered exception. No maintainer accept-note in the maintainer block authorises this specific due-date computation (the nearby Antti-2026-08-21 quote covers placement, not the freshness math).
